# Fixed controller custody repair — 2026-09-14

Repair the failed source delivery described in
`ASTRA-CONTROLLER-BOUNDARY01-SOURCE-FAILURE-2026-09-14.md`. Read that verdict,
the complete previous implementation brief, its eight-source plan, the frozen
delivery map and both final peer verdicts. This is a fresh source-only repair.
The ten previous draft cases remain unexecuted; stage95 at `fc17b67` is accepted
and must not be rerun merely to document this work.

Use the exact frozen delivery in
`docs/library/proof/controller-boundary-source-failure-2026-09-14/delivery/frozen`
and its map in the parent directory. The source pair is durable
`4eeeade5384ca8172c3724a3ee2a6574ca6801e3af3408f177e586c9cd9a4dc3` and adapter
`94e522e622b8de3304ef48c97258a91692e70f22c3112dd6afabd6b493438611`.
The original accepted adapter prefix is all 34,968 bytes of
`2f12cbf5a5f1142f892aa34df7d23af77107148b448fb4294329532e36be63ee`.
Keep that prefix, accepted fixtures/tests and actual generated source unchanged.

Coordinate one concrete interface before writing. The source author owns only
fresh `_scratch/controller-boundary-custody-repair01`; the fixture author owns
fresh `_scratch/controller-boundary-fixture-repair01`. Neither edits the other's
delivery or production files. Root integrates only reviewed frozen outputs.

The factory must retain the exact initially issued controller custody and its
startup/full-permit/raw-permit/record/token/owner relation. Both boundaries must
compare that same custody identity and current issuance, then validate current
references, values and live state. A shallow same-type custody replacement must
refuse. A controller attempt cannot become generated because its profile or
registry changes. Bind fixed canonical helpers outside the locks and retain the
original functions; a lower hook must not select the callable used later. Use
fixed internal data and direct internal calls, with no caller callback, optional
validator/module or unchecked attempt parameter. Preserve the preexisting
`start_owned_worker` signature and refuse missing/substituted controller attempt
data before lower effects. Preserve legitimate generated entry and its gates.

Keep manager-then-token lock order. The pre-resume point follows actual binding
and precedes the single resume attempt; the final point is inside the factory's
actual publication block after `finish_start`. Bind and finish hooks stay outside
both locks. A failure after worker creation must retain and stop that exact
worker while preserving the primary exception and uncertain custody through the
existing quarantine path. Real worker startup remains unconditionally closed.

Repair the new fixture and cases with before copies and a reason for each
change. Use actual canonical module imports, issuance, consumption, factory and
reservation operations over inert lower services. Put negative mutation hooks
after actual binding when testing pre-resume checks. Arm cleanup faults only
after establishing the intended primary failure. Test exact error/worker/custody
identity and real lease exit separately from simple revocation. Explicit teardown
must run on assertion failure and retain uncertainty when cleanup cannot settle.

Cover initial custody/helper/attempt substitution, both validation boundaries,
single-resume and selection changes with meaningful controls. Exercise actual
generated sentinel and owned-binding gates with positive and wrong-profile
controls; a generic fake profile is insufficient. Do not seed positive custody
or replace validators to manufacture success. Negative mutation controls may
replace inert state only to prove refusal or use of the originally fixed
authority. Keep precise case names and a frozen source-ordered case list.

Deliver complete source files, immutable before copies, valid full mechanical
diffs for each changed file and new-file diffs, actual byte/hash maps, the finite
canonical import closure with exact source paths, and a short report matching
the code. Check patch reconstruction passively without importing the subject.
Preserve every intermediate authored draft before revising it, with its reason;
never repair the original failed diff in place. No accepted assertion change is
authorized by this brief. Any failure after later admitted execution requires a
new product repair brief; do not relabel or erase it.

No Python startup, compile, import, tests or qualification harness in this unit.
No native calls, model/support/D1/D2 artifact access, physical journal, live index,
port 5179, fetch or paid API. No child transport/adoption/bootstrap, constructors,
PCM/filter/VAD/inference/diarization, packaging, installation, website or marketing.
No production edits or worker Git mutation. Review source first; prepare and
review any later guarded instrument under a separate committed brief.

Repair design only. No source implementation or execution is authorized here.

Use the accepted durable3c8963ea and adapter2f12cbf5 originals, preserving the adapter's entire34,968-byte prefix. The rejected factory4eeeade5/adapter94e522e6 and malformed diff remain diagnostic inputs, unchanged. Implement later in a fresh derivative with exact before copies and mechanical diffs. No patch to the generated delegates, reservation service or accepted95 fixtures/tests is needed.

The concrete storage is one private _DurableKernel._factory_starts dictionary, initialized empty. Only DurableOwnedRuntimeFactory.open_owned_session issues entries in normal source flow. Each raw permit identity maps to (attempt, entered), where attempt is an exact frozen _FactoryStartAttempt and entered is a Boolean. The record retains factory, manager, exact kernel/delegate, profile, full permit and original raw identity, record, owner, protection, token, and controller binding. It also retains the literal canonical adapter module and the original fixed capture/check function objects. The worker continues to live in existing kernel._starts and token.worker; do not introduce a competing worker owner.

Factory entry first resolves the literal asr_loading_adapter module and named functions after module initialization and outside state locks. It never accepts a module/function/mode argument. Under manager→token locks, validate the existing permit/record relation, perform fixed controller classification, create the actual OwnedSession as before, then register the exact attempt with entered=False. Refuse an existing entry rather than overwrite it. All potentially failing work after assigning record.owner must be inside the existing exception-preserving factory try path; an issuance failure must not leave the owner outside quarantine accounting.

Restore exactly start_owned_worker(self, protection, permit, profile). Remove the optional attempt parameter and its supplied-module path. At entry, under manager→token locks, require the dictionary entry to contain the exact attempt, entered=False, the same protection/profile/raw permit, current manager/kernel/delegate/record/token, exact factory type with factory.manager unchanged, the original full permit relation and the actual record.owner. Mark that same entry entered=True before create. Direct kernel entry without a factory-issued entry, a second entry, or a mismatched entry refuses before the delegate. The Boolean latch is consumed before the first fallible create; no retry resets it. This local registry relation is not presented as protection against arbitrary Python code rewriting private objects.

Retain the local attempt across create/bind/finish. At each new boundary, check that _factory_starts still contains that same attempt with entered=True and all its original manager/record/token/owner/protection/permit/profile/delegate relations. Immediately retain a returned worker in existing _starts before binding, as today. Before resume and publication require that exact local worker is both _starts[original_permit_identity] and token.worker. Never choose a worker by PID, attributes or a replacement current token.

Append three private adapter interfaces:

| Interface | Contract |
|---|---|
| _capture_controller_boundary(profile, full_permit) | Pure selection under the caller's manager→token locks. Return one exact frozen _ControllerBoundary for the existing issued custody, or None when there is no controller attempt. It creates no approval, session, permit or custody. |
| _validate_controller_pre_resume(startup, permit, session, worker) | Distinct predicate derived from the accepted stage checks, requiring WORKER_BOUND, resume_attempted=False and an unpublished live idle session. Existing stage methods and labels remain unchanged. |
| _check_controller_boundary(binding, startup, permit, session, worker, stage) | Pure identity check against the retained initial binding, then invokes its original pre-resume or existing finish_start validator. Only pre_resume and finish_start are supported by this new wrapper. No callback parameter. |

The controller binding retains the exact initial _StartupCustody; original custody manager/factory/record/token/lease/permit/protection; its four reference/value snapshot tuple objects; and the fixed helper identities. Require both current custody registries to retain that same initial object and relation. A copied same-type custody with equal fields must refuse. Missing/replaced registry entries, replaced snapshot tuples, changed selected records/values, revoked owner/token and a changed consumed session also refuse. The first captured binding remains controller-classified after a failure; do not create a new binding from whichever custody is current.

Keep the fixed helper set literal and finite: capture/check wrappers, pre-resume wrapper/locked predicate, accepted worker-stage wrapper/locked predicate, _startup_selection_current, _startup_references, _startup_values, _startup_authority_snapshot and _startup_configuration. Resolve and retain their original function objects; compare current named bindings before invoking the retained functions. The factory/kernel check their retained capture/check references before invoking them, so replacing the wrapper itself cannot evade the inner checks. Existing resolver/profile source guards remain in force. Do not accept a caller-selected function-name list or generic resolver. This is the reviewed fixed local call chain, not a claim of comprehensive tamper resistance for every Python global.

Classification must use existing custody for the original permit/record as well as the candidate identity. An exact _ControllerASRStart without issuance refuses; replacing a live controller attempt's profile with a dictionary, copied/foreign/subclassed record or another object refuses before create. Do not identify authority from a type name or matching attributes. If no controller attempt exists, None preserves the ordinary non-controller path only: its exact original profile is retained, and the unchanged generated delegate still validates its sentinel or _OwnedASRStart/profile/binding before effects. A later current-custody conflict must refuse, never switch the retained mode. None is not permission to start, and direct kernel calls have no factory entry and refuse for either mode.

Place pre-resume validation after successful bind_worker, inside manager→token locks held through the existing resume_owned call. Its own reentrant token lock sets resume_attempted=True exactly once before the unchanged resume callback. Keep journal work outside those locks. Before actual factory publication, retain manager→token locks through the original-binding check, the accepted finish_start validator, owner._worker assignment and NATIVE_RUNNING transition. Do not use the published predicate before those assignments, and do not treat a check at delegate return or after factory return as equivalent.

Preserve failure custody and first-error behavior. A pre-resume failure uses existing kernel revoke_local/stop_unpublished handling; a factory publication failure stops the exact returned worker while owner._worker is still None. Keep the failed attempt and consumed entry alongside existing retained state; do not erase failure evidence or clear its reservation. Do not add another stop loop. The existing caller/lease cleanup remains responsible for ordinary completion. _fixed_real_worker_start stays unconditionally closed. No real bootstrap, native handle, pipe, child, namespace or constructor authority is added.

Import/fixture decision: use a literal function-local canonical import, with no reverse top-level import and no alias change during operations. The accepted95 closure remains unchanged regression evidence. Its separately loaded startup_fixture_adapter shares canonical durable classes and therefore cannot silently qualify this new reverse dependency. New controls need their own fixed canonical module family in a separately guarded invocation, selecting these derivative sources under their actual import names. The new fixture must use actual startup issuance/consumption/factory/reservations and the inherited inert worker creation/ordinary cleanup. It may use only generated text and declared inert lower observations, with the isolated test anchor restored afterward; it must not seed either custody registry or successful ownership.

Peer fixture design identifies one necessary declared seam for exact post-bind timing: a transparent test-only wrapper calls the original ReservationService.bind_worker once, confirms its successful WORKER_BOUND/pending=None/exact-worker result, then performs one bounded mutation before returning to the real kernel. This changes the new fixture only. Label it explicitly as a wrapper, restore it in finally, and do not claim the existing sync callback occurs after binding publication. Root must review that fixture/instrument before qualification.

The new controls should prove one issued positive path through changed canonical imports, absent/replayed/foreign factory entry refusal before create, same-field custody substitution refusal, original helper replacement refusal, selection/worker/token changes after bind and after finish return, revocation with failing cleanup preserving the exact first error, and unchanged generated gate success/refusal through the changed factory. They must check actual calls/order/latches, not hand-set success fields or substitute validators. Proposed tests remain unexecuted. No additional Ryan-only decision is needed for this source unit; real activation remains closed.

No textual draft correction has been applied in this directory: this is the first written design. The preserved actual read and source pins identify its evidence; interface discussion with runtime_release_scope precedes any implementation.
